title: Ammunition: compatibility, storage and inspection
tldr: Use only ammunition confirmed for the exact firearm by its markings and manufacturer’s manual. Keep ammunition locked, dry, identifiable and away from unauthorized people; isolate uncertain or damaged rounds from use.
steps: Retain original packaging and identifying information. Do not mix loose cartridges or identify ammunition by appearance alone.

Match the manual, firearm markings and ammunition packaging. Similar names or dimensions do not establish that a cartridge is safe for a firearm. Ask the manufacturer or a qualified professional if uncertain.
Use secured storage separate from unloaded firearms. Follow manufacturer guidance on moisture, heat and storage; keep oils, solvents and water away from ammunition.
Stop using damaged or uncertain ammunition
Do not fire corroded, deformed, flooded, contaminated or unidentified ammunition. Arrange lawful disposal through qualified local channels; do not burn, dismantle or throw it into a fire.
sections: Record caliber exactly as labeled, manufacturer, lot when available, quantity and storage location in a private record. Inventory supports compatibility and accountability; it should not be posted publicly or attached to an easily shared household contact card. Review condition when checking storage, without unnecessarily manipulating cartridges.

Keep suspect ammunition separate from normal stock and restrict access. Do not try to restore wet ammunition by heating it. Disposal services and transport requirements differ; describe what you have and ask for instructions before taking suspect material to a facility.
without_help: If reliable identification or inspection is unavailable, do not use the ammunition. Securing it and postponing use is safer than guessing from an online comparison photo.
household: Keep keys, packaging and loose cartridges away from children and visitors. Include ammunition security in household relocation planning without giving untrained people responsibility for handling it.
pack_now: Keep the equipment and written information described above where the responsible person can reach them. Test access in darkness, with a tired household, and while carrying the items you actually need.
next: Audit labels and storage access. Mark anything uncertain as not for use and arrange appropriate professional advice.
watch: This guide does not provide reloading, ammunition manufacture, modification or performance optimization instructions.
review_status: Source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
scope: Civilian educational planning. References include U.S. systems; local laws, conditions and services differ.
